card_title: Even Us Up: B2B Expense Mgmt (Teams/Orgs — Long-Term)
objective: Complete Phase 1.0 implementation specification and discovery validation for B2B expense management feature targeting Canadian SMBs with 5-50 employees. Deliver fully-scoped MVP spec, risk assessment, and handoff contract ready for implementation phase.
scope_completed: Market research and competitive analysis (Expensify, Divvy, Concur, Xero, Zoho Books)
Differentiation strategy (Interac e-Transfer, CRA T5018/T776 reporting, QB/FreshBooks sync)
Phase 1.0 MVP scope (approval workflow, categorization, reporting, org management)
Detailed database schema and API endpoints
UI wireframes for employee, manager, finance views

option_a.name: HAL Parallel Dispatch (Fastest)
option_a.description: Spawn HAL to handle Phase 1.0 implementation end-to-end (backend + frontend). Alfred monitors progress and handles integration reviews.
cons: Higher risk if HAL communication breaks

option_b.name: Alfred Sequential Implementation
option_b.description: Alfred implements Phase 1.0 features sequentially (backend → frontend → testing). Proven reliability, thorough testing.
pros: Joe can provide input during development
cons: Blocks other work while in progress
Stretches to Week of May 5 launch

option_c.name: Hybrid (Alfred + HAL)
option_c.description: Alfred handles backend scaffolding + approval workflow. HAL handles frontend UI + reporting dashboard. Coordinate via daily standup.
pros: Parallelizes work while keeping core with Alfred
Faster than sequential, lower risk than pure HAL
Good balance of speed and oversight
cons: Need to define handoff points clearly

functional: Multi-tenant org creation and user management (Admin, Manager, Employee, Finance roles)
Expense submission form with categorization, date, amount, receipt upload
Finance dashboard with summary cards and expense list filtering
CSV export of expenses with date range filters
Email notifications for submission, approval, rejection
Role-based access control (employees see own expenses, managers see team, finance sees all)
non_functional: Mobile-responsive design (CSS media queries, no native app)
Database supports 1000+ concurrent users per org
All user input validated (XSS, SQL injection protection)
testing: Unit tests for approval logic, categorization, filtering (80%+ coverage)
Integration tests for API endpoints (happy path + error cases)
E2E tests for complete expense flow (submit → approve → view)
Manual testing with 5-10 pilot customers before launch

validation_commands.backend_readiness: npm run test:unit && npm run test:integration
validation_commands.frontend_readiness: npm run test:unit && npm run build
validation_commands.db_migrations: npm run migrate:up && npm run seed:test
validation_commands.success_signal: 20+ pilot orgs created, 50+ expenses submitted, NPS >30 in feedback survey

blockers_and_dependencies: No blockers identified; all tech stack decisions finalized
Dependency: AWS S3 credentials for file upload (staging + production)
Dependency: SendGrid API key for email notifications
Dependency: Stripe test account (for future Phase 2 billing, can be post-Phase-1.0)

technical.mitigation: Use row-level security (RLS) in PostgreSQL; audit schema design with security expert; test tenant isolation with e2e tests

technical.risk: Approval workflow edge cases (simultaneous approval, status conflicts)
technical.mitigation: Implement state machine (e.g., xstate); test all transitions; add idempotency keys to API

technical.risk: File upload failures (S3 unavailable, large file handling)
technical.mitigation: Implement retry logic (3 attempts, exponential backoff); user feedback UI; max file size 50MB

technical.risk: Email delivery (spam folder, bounces, rate limits)
technical.mitigation: Use SendGrid, monitor deliverability dashboard; implement email verification in signup; test with staging

business.risk: Pilot customers don't adopt (poor UX, missing features)
business.mitigation: Onboarding flow with tooltips; daily standup with pilot customers during first 2 weeks; iterate based on feedback

business.risk: Scope creep (customers request features beyond Phase 1.0)
business.mitigation: Clear scope document shared with pilots; roadmap posted publicly; feature requests go to backlog for Phase 2

communication_protocol.daily_standup: 9:00 AM AST (async update to Discord if remote)
communication_protocol.progress_updates: End-of-day summary in kanban card comments
communication_protocol.design_decisions: Post in Discord before implementation (5-minute decision window)
communication_protocol.integration_review: Joe reviews end-to-end before pilot launch (Wednesday of Week 6)

sign_off_requirements.alfred_approval: Discovery complete; handoff contract ready for HAL or Alfred implementation. Recommendation: Option A (HAL parallel) if available; Option C (hybrid) if HAL unavailable.
sign_off_requirements.joe_approval: Joe must approve one of three implementation options (A/B/C) before Phase 1.0 begins. Target approval: today (2026-03-22) for Week of April 21 ship date.

notes: This is a post-scale play with strong unit economics. Phase 1.0 MVP is achievable in 4-6 weeks with clear scope. Recommend HAL dispatch for fastest execution if Joe approves Option A. Otherwise, Alfred can execute sequentially with Joe's concurrent oversight on other cards. All discovery artifacts are in place; ready to move to implementation kanban.
